_label: MEASURED -- real Verilator RTL cosimulation of the full top-level datapath, not estimated
scope: 520,000 transactions (120,000 per mode x4 + 40,000 mixed-mode), randomized valid/ready backpressure both directions, reset-mid-stream flush test, id/mode/data checked every retirement, exact C quantizer golden vectors (rtl/tb/gen_top_x_vectors.c and friends)

b1.note: identical to baseline at this granularity -- expected: B1 only changes q4_scale's constant-divisor path, which does not change L_MAX or any latency number, exactly the claim phase-b1.md already made, re-confirmed here with per-mode instrumentation that did not previously exist.

b2.note: Q4_ENC's own mean latency (473 cycles) reflects membrane_quant_stream_top_b2.sv's full serialization discipline (only one Q4_0 encode transaction in flight at a time, blocking all other issuance -- see that file's header) PLUS the iterative divider's own ~29-cycle general-path latency PLUS q4_pack's fixed 2-cycle tail; Q8_ENC/Q8_DEC/Q4_DEC's mean latency also rose (~12 -> ~22.8 cycles) purely from occasionally queuing behind an in-flight, fully-serializing Q4_0 encode transaction -- this is the real, measured, disclosed throughput cost of Phase B2's area-first single-in-flight design point, not a bug.

throughput_cost_summary.caveat: measured at this test's specific mode mix (25% Q4 encode + 40,000 mixed-mode transactions); a real workload's actual Q4-encode fraction would change the overall ratio -- see phase-b2.md for the corresponding structural discussion, not a single universal number
